The '''Mesmes language''' is an [[extinct language|extinct]] [[West Gurage languages|West Gurage]] language, one of the [[Ethiopian Semitic languages]] spoken in [[Ethiopia]]. There are still many people who claim the Mesmes ethnic identity, but none who speak the language.  The [[Terminal speaker|last speaker]] of the language, named Abegaz, was interviewed by a [[language survey]] team when he was approximately 80 years old. He had not spoken the language for 30 years, having nobody to speak it with since his brother died.

The Mesmes have [[Language shift|shifted]] to speaking the [[Hadiyya language]]. However, they still maintain some cultural distinctives, including their own style of  house architecture.{{Citation needed|date=February 2023}}

The [[comparative method]] has shown that the language is most closely related to the [[Inor language|Inor]] variety of Gurage.<ref>Ahland (2010), p. 88</ref>

A study of the phonology of Mesmes has shown evidence of [[rhinoglottophilia]].<ref>Ahland, Michael. "Nasal spreading, rhinoglottophilia and the genesis of a non-etymological nasal consonant in Mesmes." In ''Annual Meeting of the Berkeley Linguistics Society'', vol. 31, no. 1, pp. 13-24. 2005.</ref>
